## Duration, recurrence and the phase-error timescale

- Episode duration: median 4 d, P90 14 d, max 42 d. 1.0% of episodes exceed 30 d and 0.0% exceed 60 d.
- Gap between the starts of successive episodes of the same pair: median 20 d (P10-P90 5-107 d, n=139 gaps among 64 recurring pairs).
- Section 6.3 (PHASE_CLAIMS.md) found satellite-level phase-error turning points a median 23 d apart (P10-P90 9-54 d). The episode-recurrence gap has a similar median (20 d) but a wider spread (P10-P90 5-107 d). The two characteristic intervals are of similar magnitude, but this comparison is descriptive rather than evidence of a common process; it is not a claim that a specific reversal causes a specific episode, since the pair-level gap and the satellite-level turning point are different units measured on different (though overlapping) samples.
- No episode exceeds 42 d, and only 1.0% exceed 30 d. Section 6.2 found the correlation of a satellite's signed phase error with its own earlier value falls to 0.47 at 30 d and to about 0 by 60 d (satellites on grid at least 90 d after arrival). The comparable timescales do not establish an explanation for episode termination, since episode persistence depends on pair-level geometry (Section 8) as well as the phase-error process; the observed scarcity of episodes beyond about a month is reported as an empirical property of the record, not attributed directly to phase-error decorrelation.
